topic_tag: a pamphlet and a tenants' movement
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Looking back, one historian called the pamphlet the movement's ______ in its first decade.

worlds.passage: In 1882 a forty-page pamphlet on the rights of tenant farmers appeared in one rural province, the same year a tenants' movement formed there. Its chapters covered calling a meeting, wording a petition to a landlord, and filing a complaint with the county court. Branches of the movement kept copies on the table at every meeting and turned to the matching chapter as each item of business came up, and members wrote corrections into the margins wherever a court's procedure had changed, mailing them to the printer for the next edition. Looking back, one historian called the pamphlet the movement's ______ in its first decade.
worlds.explanation: Branches opened the pamphlet to the relevant chapter as each item of business arose and kept its procedures current, so it served as the movement's "handbook," a practical guide in daily use. "Gospel" fails because members corrected it freely rather than treating it as beyond question. "Foil" fails because the movement relied on the pamphlet rather than defining itself against it. "Fundraiser" fails because its value lay in being consulted, not in money raised from it.

gospel.quote: members wrote corrections into the margins
gospel.why: a text members routinely correct is not treated as unquestionable doctrine

foil.quote: kept copies on the table at every meeting
foil.why: the movement relied on the pamphlet, so it was not a contrasting text to argue against

fundraiser.why: what mattered was its content in use at meetings, not any income it produced

worlds.passage: In 1882 a forty-page pamphlet on the rights of tenant farmers appeared in one rural province, the same year a tenants' movement formed there. Its author, a village schoolteacher, argued in one unbroken essay that land belongs by right to those who work it, and the movement's speakers quoted its sentences as final whenever members disagreed about what the movement stood for. When a branch secretary published an essay in 1887 questioning one of its claims, his branch expelled him within the month, and no member criticized the pamphlet in print again before 1892. Looking back, one historian called the pamphlet the movement's ______ in its first decade.
worlds.explanation: Its sentences were quoted as final in disputes over aims, and questioning it got a member expelled and silenced all later criticism, so the pamphlet was the movement's "gospel," a doctrine accepted without question. "Handbook" fails because it was a single essay of principle, used to say what the movement believed rather than how to do anything. "Foil" fails because the movement embraced the pamphlet instead of defining itself against it. "Fundraiser" fails because it was valued for its authority, not for money.

handbook.why: an essay of principle offers no practical procedures to follow

foil.why: the movement treated the pamphlet as its authority, the reverse of a text it opposed

fundraiser.quote: his branch expelled him within the month
fundraiser.why: the pamphlet's importance was as untouchable doctrine, not as a source of income

worlds.passage: In 1882 a forty-page pamphlet on the rights of tenant farmers appeared in one rural province, the same year a tenants' movement formed there. Its author, a landowner, argued that tenants already held every right they could fairly claim. The movement's speakers read its sentences aloud at rallies before setting out their own demands against them, and the movement's first written program listed, one by one, the very rights the pamphlet had said tenants did not need. Looking back, one historian called the pamphlet the movement's ______ in its first decade.
worlds.explanation: Written by a landowner against tenants' claims, the pamphlet gave the movement something to set its demands against, down to a program built from the rights it had denied, so it was the movement's "foil," the contrast that defined it. "Handbook" fails because the movement contradicted the pamphlet rather than following it. "Gospel" fails because the movement rejected its argument. "Fundraiser" fails because nothing suggests it raised money for the movement.

handbook.quote: the very rights the pamphlet had said tenants did not need
handbook.why: the movement's program asserted what the pamphlet denied, the reverse of following its guidance

gospel.quote: setting out their own demands against them
gospel.why: the speakers opposed its sentences, so it was not their accepted doctrine

fundraiser.why: it was an opponent's argument, used for contrast, not something the movement sold for funds

worlds.passage: In 1882 a forty-page pamphlet on the rights of tenant farmers appeared in one rural province, the same year a tenants' movement formed there. Its pages repeated arguments already made in every newspaper in the province, and copies found in members' homes decades later are mostly uncut beyond the first few leaves. The movement printed it in runs of twenty thousand, members sold copies for a penny at fairs and markets, and the proceeds paid the rent of the halls where its branches met and the fees of lawyers who defended evicted tenants. Looking back, one historian called the pamphlet the movement's ______ in its first decade.
worlds.explanation: Its arguments were familiar and its pages largely unopened, while huge penny runs paid for halls and lawyers, so the pamphlet was the movement's "fundraiser." "Handbook" fails because its pages held arguments, not procedures, and most copies were never opened past the start. "Gospel" fails because a pamphlet repeating commonplace arguments, left unread, was not the movement's revered authority. "Foil" fails because the movement printed and sold it itself rather than arguing against it.

handbook.quote: repeated arguments already made in every newspaper
handbook.why: its content was general argument, not practical guidance

gospel.quote: mostly uncut beyond the first few leaves
gospel.why: a text whose pages were never opened was not treated as sacred authority

foil.quote: The movement printed it in runs
foil.why: the movement produced and sold the pamphlet, so it was not a text it defined itself against
